sketches.name: Returning Court
sketches.idea: A folded perimeter turns around a common court; its increasing depth becomes the expression.
sketches.approach: Plan-like enclosing fold with open entrance
sketches.reason: Gathered interior is visible. A cog, wreath or enclosing fortress remains possible; the tapering seams are too complex for a lead mark.

sketches.name: One Fold
sketches.idea: One strip folds around an interior and then rises beyond its own enclosure.
sketches.reason: One continuous object carries dwelling and movement. The interlocking corners can read as packaging, recycling or a technology loop.

sketches.name: Answering Surfaces
sketches.idea: Two folded surfaces answer across one shared interior; each helps make the room.
sketches.reason: Large counter and directional weight are clear. At first glance it may be an abstract leaf pair, split flame or rotational industry mark.

sketches.name: Opening Measure
sketches.idea: A stable architectural mass progressively opens, so its own structure becomes generous.
sketches.reason: The carved mass has a strong edge but the wedge/roof silhouette still suggests contemporary property or a sculptural building.

sketches.name: Processional Fold
sketches.idea: A horizontal gathering becomes one broad rising return, expressing praise through movement.
sketches.approach: Low pleated procession and rising sweep
sketches.reason: The sweep is kinetic and changes the axis of the original. Jagged peaks can suggest mountains, a sports brand or an upward chart.

sketches.name: Common Vault
sketches.idea: Unequal folded shells join around one interior rather than stand as individual pillars.
sketches.reason: The most unified shell construction, with cadence around a room. Could read as a folded rosette, aperture or abstract flame; avoid overclaiming immediate church recognition.

developed.name: Opening Measure
developed.idea: A single folded wall enlarges its openings as it turns around a shared interior; the dwelling itself supplies the cadence.
developed.visible: A joined sloping surface, two measured cuts and one generous interior open through the lower edge. Angular left faces answer a curved outer return.
developed.meaning: The same structural gesture makes room and expresses movement. Joined construction suggests a shared dwelling; changing intervals and an expansive return suggest collective response. These are contemporary design associations, not a historical reconstruction or an image of divine presence.
construction: One upper diagonal joins every zone. The two cuts sit below it with substantial material bridges instead of dividing the mark into separate pillars.
Small intervals lead toward a larger shared interior. The lower threshold is genuinely open, replacing v3’s pinched point contact.
Angular folded faces on the left contrast with a broad curved return on the right. All cuts are real negative space in one filled compound path.
developed.risk: The primary association can still be a sculptural building or product emblem. A residual flame-like reading is possible in the large interior. Christian parish meaning needs the complete name and context; the artwork alone does not make it explicit.
developed.smallSize: Native 16 px retains the sloping silhouette and open interior, while the finer upper interval largely merges. At 24 px the folded structure is identifiable; at 32 px the measured cuts are clearer. White reverse retains the threshold but looks slightly heavier at tiny sizes. Use 32 px or larger when the full cadence matters.
developed.longevity: The identity rests on a structural silhouette and the relationship of solid to space, without a transient effect. Long-term usefulness is plausible, but church warmth and the sculptural/property association need congregation review.
developed.selectionReason: E4 gives the strongest connection between architectural rhythm and a shared interior. E1/E2 read as loops or packaging; E3 reads as a split flame or rotation; E5 retains peaks and chart associations; E6 approaches an aperture. V4 repairs v3’s fragile upper ties and common bottom point without restarting the concept. Extra investigation does not make E the strongest of the five directions.
